title: A Practical Guide to Phage- and Robotics-assisted Near-continuous Evolution
protocol: Obtain the primary hardware for the PRANCE system.
Include a liquid handling instrument with an 8-channel pipetting arm and a single-piston 96-tip pipetting arm.
Equip the system with a robotic gripper for moving plates.
Integrate an automated wash station for tip sterilization.
Install an integrated plate reader capable of absorbance and luminescence measurements.
Configure heating strategies based on the liquid handling robot model.
Use a heated plate carrier or heater-mediated climate control for temperature maintenance.
Establish a tip-wash station to allow for tip reuse.
Establish a source of bacterial culture maintained at log-phase by setting up a real-time bioreactor running at 37 °C as a chemostat/turbidostat.
Alternatively, arrest a log-phase bacterial culture of at least 1 L volume pre-grown at 37 °C in log-phase (OD600 between 0.25 and 0.45) at 4 °C in a nearby refrigerator.
Stir the arrested culture regularly using a shaker plate or stir plate to prevent sedimentation.
Configure the preferred pumps for robotic integration with necessary software and drivers.
Implement software to enable pumps to deliver defined quantities of liquid on the order of 10-100 mL.

Set up a three-pump manifold capable of pumping three separate channels: delivering bacteria to bacterial reservoir, delivering bleach to bacterial reservoir, and draining bacterial reservoir to waste.
Calibrate and control the speed of each pump independently.
Use a robot gripper to transfer plates in or out of the reader.
Initiate a plate reader measurement.
Access measurements.
3D-print the bacterial reservoir/distribution manifold ("waffle").
Secure the printed components onto the deck of the Liquid Handling Robot.
Calibrate the positions of the containers using standard Liquid Handling Robot software.
Connect the reservoir to the pump array.
Install open-source software used for controlling Liquid Handling robots with python.
Modify and calibrate the deck layout file in the robot software to reflect the labware positions accurately.
Open the Command Line with Windows key + R.
Enter: cmd in the Run dialog box.
Change the parent directory to c:\Robot_methods_directory\PRANCE using CD command.
Call the robot method program in simulation mode with Python and the simulate flag: py robot_method.py --simulate.
Select the PLAY button in the Robot Run Control window.
Run the PRANCE robot method program without simulation mode by opening Command Line.
Enter: cmd in the Run dialog box.
Change the parent directory to c:\Robot_methods_directory\PRANCE using CD command.
Call the robot method program with Python without flags: py robot_method.py.
Select the PLAY button in the upper left of the Robot Run Control window.
Confirm that PyHamilton can control the instrument and cause it to initialize.
Establish real-time data synchronization.
Ensure log-phase bacterial culture sources are available for all cultures required for the planned run.
Actively stir bacterial cultures to prevent sedimentation.
Use an active chemostat/turbidostat or a growth-arrested refrigerated pregrown culture.
Update the controller manifest file with details of volume (range 0-500 µL) and bacterial culture for each well of the 96-well lagoon per program cycle.
Calculate the dilution rate of the lagoon using DilutionCalculator.xlsx spreadsheet.
Update the robot_method.py file with 14 as the value for fixed_lagoon_height.
Place clean filtered pipette tips onto the robot deck in their designated positions.
Tape the tip racks to the tip holders to ensure stability during the run.
Place clean 96-deep-well plates onto the robot deck in their designated positions.
Place clean 96-well reader plates onto the robot deck in their designated positions.
Ensure that the plate reader tray is not occupied by a pre-existing plate.
Connect pumps to the computer and assign them to the correct address.
Clean pump lines by activating pumps to pump bleach, followed by water.
Connect pump lines to the appropriate sources and outputs for bacterial cultures.
Refill tanks/buckets containing bleach/water for bacterial reservoir and pipette tip washing.
Ensure all on-deck components, particularly mobile elements, are stabilized in their designated positions.
Activate heaters as per local implementation to target temperature (e.g., 37 °C).
Run the UV Sterilization Protocol file for 10 min.
Select the PLAY button in the upper left of the Robot Run Control window.
Execute the file with the parametrized option for 600 s.
Close the Robot Run Control software after execution.
Conduct a 'water run' overnight using the PRANCE robot method program.
Substitute water for all cultures and wet reagents during the water run.
Set up pre-run preparation as detailed above with controller_manifest and robot_method.
Use an effective lagoon dilution rate of 1 volume/h.
Connect the 'bacteria in' line to a container of water.
Add food coloring to the water sources to track liquid movement through the experiment.
Open the Command Line in the appropriate directory.
Call the robot method program with Python using the new run flag (py robot_method.py --new).

Input the requested arguments, including log file name (TestRun), number of lagoon wells (16), cycle duration (30), number of cycles per reader plate measurement (4), and inducer volume (inducer volume is 0 µL for this test run).
Select the PLAY button in the upper left of the Robot Run Control window that will open once arguments have been provided.
Conduct a 'bacteria-only run', where the PRANCE protocol is run overnight only with bacterial culture at target temperature but with no bacteriophage.
Ensure that heaters are switched on for a target temperature of 37 °C.
Connect the 'bacteria in' line to the selected source of log-phase bacteria.
Call the robot method program with Python using the new run flag (py robot_method.py --new).
Input the requested arguments as detailed previously in section 4.1.4.
Select the PLAY button in the upper left of the Robot Run Control window that opens when the program is executed after providing arguments.
Run an 'infection test' where phages bearing an evolved protein are challenged to propagate on bacteria requiring that protein.
Decide in advance which lagoons will be inoculated with phage and which will serve as no-phage control lagoons for detecting cross-contamination.
Complete the pre-run preparation using the controller_manifest and robot_method set up for an effective dilution rate of 1 volume/h, as shown in Figure 5 and Figure 6.
Ensure that heaters are switched on to maintain a target temperature of 37 °C.
Connect the 'bacteria in' line to the selected source of log-phase bacteria.
Open the Command Line in the appropriate directory.
Before adding bacteriophage, run the method for 2-3 h to equilibrate the volume and bacteria OD in the lagoon plates.
Inoculate the with-phage lagoons with 106 pfu/mL of bacteriophage at the end of a run cycle when the program is sleeping.
Add 5.5 µL of phage aliquot at 108 pfu/mL into a 550 µL lagoon.
Run the program overnight.
Check the phage titer in the lagoon wells by plaque assay or qPCR.
